criteria.check: Read metrics.py and graph.draft: all figures are computed in metrics.compute and the model only receives the rendered table. But the guard (the only enforcement that memo figures came from metrics.py) misses spelled-out amounts and numerals preceded by '.' or followed by letters, so a model-originated figure can reach a 'grounded' memo.
Read every Metric constructor; each carries evidence ids. Tests test_every_metric_cites_evidence and test_evidence_reproduces_each_figure pass (94 passed).

Traced the draft prompt: account name (always 'Applicant' from ingest), period, metrics table (name/display/method are code constants) and policy rule text from YAML. No transaction descriptions reach the drafting model, so statement-description prompt injection into the memo graph is not possible. (The MCP server is a separate path that does return raw descriptions to an LLM client; see findings.)
Probed guard.check with invented figures appended to a grounded memo: 'c.48k', 'forty-eight thousand pounds' and '48250pounds' all return grounded=True.

Read the review interrupt, ReviewDecision and the CLI. `cma run --yes --reviewer X` records an approval by X before any human has read the memo; reviewer is an unauthenticated free-text string and '   ' (whitespace) is accepted.

Rules are deterministic and ordered, and a credit that matches no rule is OTHER. But the rule `^FPS CREDIT` labels every inbound Faster Payment as revenue whoever sent it. Owner round-trip probe: £6k a month out as drawings and straight back in by FPS (net cash zero) adds £72k of revenue and moves DSCR from 1.43 to 6.65, flipping policy R2 from refer to pass.
Thresholds, ops, on_fail and refer bands all come from YAML (yaml.safe_load); policy.py holds only the operator map.

Regenerated each committed CSV (examples/ and evals/results/statements/) from synth.generate with its truth seed/months; all 10 are byte-identical, so they are synthetic. Grep for secrets, keys, employer names, sort codes and account numbers: none. Two counterparties are real UK businesses, contrary to the 'fictional' comment, and nothing stops a real statement being committed.

Read ingest.load_csv: checks missing columns, empty id, duplicate id, ISO date, finite amount/balance and running balance, then raises StatementError before anything is computed; the CLI exits with code 2. The parametrised tests in test_ingest pass.
The CI workflow references no secrets; get_llm defaults to FakeLLM; evals run with --llm fake.

Property probe: 9 archetype/profile cases x seeds 1-40 x months {6,12,13} = 1080 statements; 8 M5 mismatches (e.g. trades/good seed 1: M5 17327.55 vs truth 14000.0). The existing test only covers seed 7.
Same probe as R4: spelled-out amounts and numerals next to '.' or letters are never scanned, so they are not flagged.

findings.claim: Every inbound Faster Payment (`^FPS CREDIT`) and any credit whose text contains `INV<digits>` is categorised as trading revenue, whoever sent it. An owner moving money back in, a director's loan, a refund or a transfer from savings all count as revenue and as operating inflow. metrics.py:46 excludes owner drawings from operating cash flow but has no matching treatment for owner money coming back in. So an applicant can round-trip cash to inflate revenue and DSCR: this is a known fraud pattern in the money path.
findings.repro: Take examples/cafe_stretched.csv. Once a month insert 'TFR OWNER DRAWINGS -6000.00' then 'FPS CREDIT A OWNER SAVINGS +6000.00' on the same day, and re-walk the balances (script: scratchpad/panel02/security/probe_roundtrip.py). Before: M2 265368.87, M9 19721.52, M10 1.43, R2=refer. After: M2 337368.87, M9 91721.52, M10 6.65, R2=pass. Net cash moved is zero.

findings.claim: The NUMBER regex skips any numeral preceded by '.' or a letter, or followed by a letter, and it has no handling for spelled-out numbers. An invented figure written as 'c.48k', '48250pounds' or 'forty-eight thousand pounds' passes the grounding check, so the memo is presented as grounded and `--yes` will approve it.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from pathlib import Path;from cma import ingest,categorise,metrics,guard;ms=metrics.compute(categorise.categorise(ingest.load_csv(Path('examples/cafe_stretched.csv'))));[print(x,guard.check('Total revenue was £265,369 [M2]. Stock is worth '+x+'.',ms).grounded) for x in ['c.48k','48250pounds','forty-eight thousand pounds','£48,250']]" -> True, True, True, False

findings.claim: `--yes` builds an approval {'approved': True, 'reviewer': <flag>} as soon as the memo is grounded, before any person has read the draft. The final memo then says 'APPROVED by <name>' for a decision no human made. The reviewer is a free-text, unauthenticated string, so anyone who can run the CLI (a cron job, CI, an agent) can finalise a memo in any analyst's name. R5 requires a recorded human decision.
findings.repro: cma run examples/cafe_stretched.csv --yes --reviewer 'Head of Credit' --out memo.md -> memo.md ends with 'APPROVED by Head of Credit at ...' and no prompt ever appeared. With the guard bypass above, the same command also approves a memo containing 'forty-eight thousand pounds'.

findings.claim: reviewer has min_length=1 but whitespace is not stripped, and cli.py:50 tests only truthiness, so an approval with reviewer '   ' is accepted and stamped 'APPROVED by    '.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from cma.models import ReviewDecision;print(repr(ReviewDecision(approved=True,reviewer='   ').reviewer))" -> '   '; also: cma run examples/cafe_stretched.csv --yes --reviewer '   '

findings.claim: No MCP tool restricts its path argument to an allowed root, and there is no caller check beyond stdio access. compute_metrics(path) returns M1's evidence, which is every transaction id, and transactions_for(path, ids) then returns every row with its raw description. Any statement-shaped CSV the server process can read is fully readable by the client, and attacker-influenced description text goes straight to an LLM client (Claude Desktop, n8n) without being marked untrusted: a prompt-injection channel the memo graph avoids. Error text that contains file contents (a header line such as a .env 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...', or a YAML parser error quoting the line) is kept from the client only because mcp 2.2.0 hides non-ToolError exceptions. pyproject.toml:54 allows mcp>=2.0, so other versions are not verified.
findings.repro: python3 -I scratchpad/panel02/security/probe_mcp.py: statement_summary('<dir>/.env') raises StatementError '(found: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-FAKE-SECRET-123)'; compute_metrics('/etc/passwd') raises '(found: root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash)'. Over MCPServer.call_tool on 2.2.0 the client sees only 'Error executing tool statement_summary' (probe_mcp_wire.py). transactions_for('examples/cafe_stretched.csv', ['T00001','T00002']) returns full rows.

findings.claim: The workflow sets no `permissions:` block, so the GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repository default (write on many repos for push to main). Actions are pinned to mutable tags (@v4/@v5), not SHAs. Dependencies install from unpinned floors (pip install -e '.[dev,mcp]').
findings.repro: Read .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 8-21: there is no permissions key; 'uses: actions/checkout@v4' and 'actions/setup-python@v5'.

findings.claim: The synthetic counterparties include real UK businesses, 'PARCELFORCE WORLDWIDE' (line 52) and 'PLUMBWORLD' (line 41), while line 23 says they are fictional. No personal data is involved, but a public repo shows named real firms in invented bank statements.

Nothing stops a real statement being committed. .gitignore does not exclude statement CSVs outside out/ and evals/results/; `cma generate` writes into the tracked examples/ by default (cli.py:30); and CI does not check that every committed CSV regenerates from synth. The pilot step that runs a lender's anonymised statement has no technical guard.
findings.repro: cp <lender statement>.csv examples/ && pytest -q && ruff check -> CI stays green. A check that regenerates each examples/*.csv from its truth.json (as in scratchpad/panel02/security/probe_synth.py) would catch it.

findings.claim: The generator's lowest_balance truth is seeded with the opening balance, which is not a statement line. M5 is the minimum over transaction balances. When the account never dips below its opening balance, truth and M5 disagree, so P1 fails for some seeds. The test only exercises seed 7.
findings.repro: python3 -I scratchpad/panel02/security/probe_p1.py -> '1080 statements, 8 mismatches', e.g. trades/good seed=1 months=12: M5 17327.55 vs truth 14000.0
